name: Padlock Shim Attack
description: Padlock shims are thin aluminum inserts pushed into the shackle slot of a padlock, releasing the shackle without a key or picking. The shim depresses the locking pawl that holds the shackle in place. Most single-locking padlocks are vulnerable; double-locking padlocks require two shims inserted simultaneously. Shims are disposable, fast, and require no skill — making them one of the highest return-on-investment bypass tools for anyone regularly encountering padlocked gates, cages, or equipment rooms.

blue.det: Shim visible in shackle slot; padlock opens without key; camera coverage of padlock location.
blue.cm: Shrouded shackle padlocks prevent shim access; use closed-shackle padlocks for high-security applications; lock boxes or hasps protecting shackle.
